_readonly_uri (sql_runner.py:81-87) yields: relative -> 'file:rel.db?mode=ro' (no '//' so no authority parsing); absolute '/abs.db' -> 'file:/abs.db?mode=ro'; path starting '//' (e.g. '//tmp/x.db') -> 'file://' + '//tmp/x.db' = 'file:////tmp/x.db?mode=ro'; Windows drive -> 'file:///C:/x.db?mode=ro'. Per SQLite URI grammar (sqlite3ParseUri), after 'file:' a '//' introduces an authority that runs to the next '/'; it must be empty or 'localhost', otherwise 'invalid uri authority'. In 'file:////tmp' and 'file:///C:' the authority is empty, so accepted; the remaining path is '//tmp/x.db' or '/C:/x.db'. The non-'//' forms have no authority. connect_sqlite passes uri=True (line 104). Percent-encoding with safe='/' leaves the authority structure unchanged. No form triggers the error.

_readonly_uri (sql_runner.py:70-87) has three branches. Drive path (regex ^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]) gives file:///C:<quoted>?mode=ro, so the authority is empty. Path starting '//' gives file:// + quote(path), e.g. '//host/share/x.db' becomes file:////host/share/x.db, an empty authority with the path '//host/share/x.db'. '///x.db' becomes file://///x.db, also empty authority. Any other path gives file:<quoted> with no '//' after the scheme: a single-slash path is file:/abs, a relative path is file:rel, and the empty string is file:?mode=ro. For 'C:\x.db', quote encodes the backslash to %5C, giving file:///C:%5Cx.db, so there is no host. Backslash UNC paths such as '\\host\x' are percent-encoded and so cannot form an authority. I found no input that produces a host part, so the docstring claim holds.

preflight.py:76-79 wraps Path(path).absolute() in try/except OSError, falling back to '(working directory unavailable)'. The os.getcwd() decoding uses surrogateescape, so UnicodeDecodeError is not expected. This rests on my knowledge of CPython; I did not read the stdlib source in this environment.
